- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 70), model often overshoots in the following days; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or use lagged mean reversion.  
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in the 10–15 day horizon; apply a 3–5 day smoothing filter or use 14-day moving average as baseline.  
- In 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-cycle momentum; adjust final 5–7 days upward if sentiment remains positive and price is trending upward.  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift within 3–5 days.
